paper_summary: Collaguazo et al. (Engineering Solid Mechanics 8, 2020, 77-82) fill Nomex honeycomb cores with an epoxy / 3M K1 hollow glass microsphere syntactic foam (0, 20, 30 and 40 vol% microspheres) and close them with 3K carbon fibre face sheets. Three-point bending per ASTM D7264/D7264M-15 (5 specimens per group) and gravity impact tests per ASTM D3763-18 (drop heights 50 and 115 cm) were performed. Adding microspheres cut sandwich weight by 8.6-9.9% and raised specific flexural strength, with an optimum at 30 vol% (71.67 vs 55.1 for the unfilled reference, about 30% higher); specific stiffness fell for all filled groups relative to the microsphere-free material.

extraction_notes: SCOPE CAVEAT: the specimens are complete sandwich panels (3K carbon-fibre skins + Nomex honeycomb core whose cells are filled with the epoxy/3M K1 glass-microsphere syntactic foam). All reported mechanical values are structural properties of that sandwich, NOT properties of the syntactic foam itself, so they are not directly comparable to bulk syntactic-foam data. UNITS: deformation at break converted from % to fraction (2.00%, 2.17%, 3.31%, 2.14% -> 0.0200, 0.0217, 0.0331, 0.0214). MAIN AMBIGUITY: Table 1 reports an absolute 'Ultimate strength (Mpa)' only for the microsphere-free NOMEX+RESIN group (average 55.1 MPa). For the 20/30/40 vol% groups the column header is 'Ultimate strength f(% Weight Mpa)' and the conclusions call the value 'MPa/kg', i.e. a weight-normalised specific strength with units that cannot be reconciled with the schema's MPa or MPa per g/cm3. Those averages are 64.8846616 (20%), 71.6750053 (30%) and 64.9628796 (40%). They were therefore recorded in specimen_notes and evidence only, with strength_mpa and specific_strength_mpa_per_g_cc left null rather than guessed. Back-calculating an absolute strength from the stated 8.57%/9.86% weight reductions would require assumptions the paper does not state, so it was not done. Individual specimen values (five rows per group, all labelled MI-FLX-18) are given in the evidence quotes; one record per composition uses the group average. Flexural modulus/stiffness is discussed only through Fig. 3 ('specific stiffness vs volumetric fraction') with no numeric values, so modulus_mpa is null everywhere. Composite density was never measured; only the relative weight reductions (8.57% at 20 vol%, 9.86% at 30 and 40 vol%) are given, and they are recorded in microstructure_notes. Impact test records (ASTM D3763-18, 50 x 50 x 6.85 mm, drop heights 50 and 115 cm) carry no schema-mappable property: only striker displacements at h = 115 cm are quoted (1.43 mm at 20%, 1.14 mm at 30%, 2.57 mm at 40%), recorded in specimen_notes. No result is given for the 50 cm drop height or for a 0 vol% impact specimen, so no records were created for those. Test temperature was not stated for the mechanical tests (left null); the 20 C on the resin record is the datasheet's density reference temperature. Microsphere data from Table 3: 3M K1, true density 0.125 g/cm3, D50 = 65 um, compressive/crush strength 1.7 MPa (= 250 psi). Cure: oven 1 h at 154 C, 2.5 C/min ramp; foam vacuum-degassed at about 70 kPa in three cycles before casting.
